description: Birth, four sights, enlightenment, first sermon, mahaparinirvana, key locations

questions.stem: Gautama Buddha was born in which year (traditional date) and at which place?

options.option_text: 563 BCE at Lumbini, Nepal (then Kapilavastu's territory)

questions.explanation: Traditional date — 563 BCE (some sources 480 BCE). Born at LUMBINI (in modern Nepal, near Indo-Nepal border) under a sal tree. Mother Mahamaya, father Suddhodana (King of the Shakya clan). Childhood name — Siddhartha Gautama. Lumbini is a UNESCO WHS (1997) — the actual birthplace marked by Ashoka's pillar (~249 BCE) bearing inscription confirming it. Bodh Gaya is where ENLIGHTENMENT happened, not birth. Kushinagar is where he died.

questions.stem: The 'Four Sights' that prompted Siddhartha to renounce his princely life were:

options.option_text: An old man, a sick man, a corpse, and a wandering ascetic

questions.explanation: While Siddhartha lived in palace luxury (insulated from suffering by his father), he encountered FOUR SIGHTS during chariot rides outside: 1. An old, frail man (suffering of aging), 2. A diseased man (suffering of illness), 3. A dead body (mortality), 4. A serene wandering ascetic (path to liberation). These triggered his renunciation ('Mahabhinishkramana' = the Great Going Forth) at age 29. Six years of asceticism followed before enlightenment.

questions.stem: Buddha attained enlightenment (Sambodhi) under a Bodhi tree at:
questions.explanation: Bodh Gaya (Gaya district, Bihar) — Buddha sat under a Pipal (Ficus religiosa) tree on the banks of the Niranjana river. After 49 days of meditation, attained enlightenment at age 35. The original tree died; the present Mahabodhi tree is a descendant. UNESCO WHS 1992. Mahabodhi Temple was built on the spot. Sarnath — first sermon ('Dhammachakkappavattana'). Lumbini — birth. Kushinagar — death (mahaparinirvana).

questions.stem: Buddha delivered his first sermon ('Dhammachakra Pravartana' = turning the wheel of law) at:
questions.explanation: Sarnath — near Varanasi, UP — site of Buddha's first sermon to his five former companions (Pancha-Vargiya: Kondanna, Bhaddiya, Vappa, Mahanama, Assaji), who became the first Sangha. The sermon expounded the Four Noble Truths and the Noble Eightfold Path. Ashoka built the famous LION CAPITAL pillar here (now India's National Emblem). Sarnath is among the four major Buddhist pilgrimage sites — Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Kushinagar (the LBSK quartet).

questions.stem: The 'Eightfold Path' taught by Buddha is the route to:

options.option_text: Cessation of suffering (Dukkha-Nirodha) leading to Nirvana

questions.explanation: Eightfold Path (Ariya Atthangika Magga) — the 4th of the Four Noble Truths, the practical way out of suffering. Eight components: Right View, Right Intention, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, Right Concentration. Often grouped into three: Wisdom (View, Intention), Ethical Conduct (Speech, Action, Livelihood), Mental Discipline (Effort, Mindfulness, Concentration). Symbolised by the 8-spoke Dharmachakra (the Indian flag's central wheel).

questions.stem: Buddha attained Mahaparinirvana (death) at the age of 80 at:
questions.explanation: Kushinagar (Kasia, eastern UP) — Buddha's mahaparinirvana ~483 BCE under twin sal trees. Cause of death said to be food poisoning from offering by a blacksmith named Cunda (debated — could have been pork or mushroom). Mahaparinirvana Temple houses a 6.10-m-long reclining Buddha statue. Sravasti — capital of Kosala kingdom; Buddha spent 25 monsoons of his teaching career there. Rajgir — capital of Magadha; Vaishali — capital of Lichchhavis.

questions.stem: The 'Tripitaka' — the canonical scripture of Theravada Buddhism — has three baskets. They are:

options.option_text: Vinaya Pitaka, Sutta Pitaka, Abhidhamma Pitaka

questions.explanation: Tripitaka (Pali) / Tripitaka (Sanskrit) — 'Three Baskets'. Vinaya Pitaka — monastic code (rules for monks/nuns). Sutta Pitaka — sermons / discourses of Buddha and disciples. Abhidhamma Pitaka — philosophical analysis. Composed in Pali (Theravada). Mahayana also has Sanskrit canon. Compiled at successive Buddhist Councils — 1st at Rajgir (after Buddha's death), 2nd at Vaishali, 3rd at Pataliputra (Ashoka), 4th at Kashmir (Kanishka).
